citation: Heorhiadi et al. (2016), Gremlin: Systematic Resilience Testing of Microservices
system_studied: operational microservice applications; IBM enterprise application case
automation_mechanism: application-level fault injection and assertion checking
operational_context: testing and operationally relevant microservice environments
fault_or_incident_model: network and application-level failure scenarios; correlated failure chains
empirical_method: controlled experiments plus industrial case study
data_source: Gremlin framework, public source code and case-study application
participants_or_subjects: developers are discussed as users; no participant sample reported
metrics_or_outcomes: low overhead; execution speed; discovery of unhandled corner-case failures
human_factors: learning curve and operator feedback discussed qualitatively; no validated workload/trust measure
reproducibility_information: public source code is identified; exact environment/configuration and all evaluation data require extraction
limitations_or_scope: resilience-testing evaluation; not a comparison of production recovery strategies

citation: Chen et al. (2019), Continuous Incident Triage for Large-Scale Online Service Systems
automation_mechanism: automated continuous incident triage using DeepCT
fault_or_incident_model: real incident assignments and discussion histories
empirical_method: industrial operational-data study plus model evaluation
data_source: incident records and discussion data from eight systems
participants_or_subjects: on-call engineers are operational subjects; no direct participant sample
metrics_or_outcomes: reassignment proportion; discussion-item count; triage model performance
human_factors: workflow evidence only; no direct workload, trust or decision-rationale instrument
reproducibility_information: study context, systems and data source are reported; proprietary data and model configuration limit independent replication
limitations_or_scope: single organisation; automated triage outcome is not automated recovery or causal engineer-performance evidence

citation: Brogi et al. (2022), Self-healing trans-cloud applications
system_studied: Softcare trans-cloud application with multiple components and dependencies
automation_mechanism: automated monitoring, recovery planning and component self-healing
fault_or_incident_model: application-component and cloud-service failures, including unforeseen failures; monkey testing
empirical_method: prototype evaluation with controlled experiments and long-running monkey testing
data_source: open-source prototype, controlled scenarios and chaos monkey
participants_or_subjects: no human participants; system is the subject
metrics_or_outcomes: recovery of application and cloud-service failures; downtime/instability periods; scenario outcomes
reproducibility_information: open-source prototype and TOSCA application specification are reported; exact scripts/data require extraction
limitations_or_scope: trans-cloud platform and prototype assumptions limit transferability to a transactional Kubernetes CD system

citation: Chen et al. (2024), Automatic Root Cause Analysis via Large Language Models for Cloud Incidents
system_studied: Microsoft cloud services and incident-handling system
automation_mechanism: automated diagnostic-information collection, root-cause classification and explanatory narrative generation
fault_or_incident_model: real incident dataset covering one year; alert-type incident handlers
empirical_method: operational dataset plus model evaluation and deployment report
data_source: one year of Microsoft incidents; operational deployment evidence
participants_or_subjects: on-call engineers are users/operational subjects; no participant experiment
metrics_or_outcomes: RCA accuracy up to 0.766; component use in Microsoft for more than four years; root-cause prediction deployment for several months
human_factors: paper discusses manual effort and information overload but does not report direct workload or decision-quality measures
reproducibility_information: incident-handler workflow and dataset context are described; proprietary data/model evolution limit replication
limitations_or_scope: model accuracy and deployment are not evidence of causal improvement in engineer decisions, workload or service recovery

citation: Assad et al. (2024), Can My Microservice Tolerate an Unreliable Database? Resilience Testing with Fault Injection and Visualization
system_studied: microservice applications using SQL/NoSQL database clients
automation_mechanism: database-client fault injection integrated with Filibuster and an IDE plugin
fault_or_incident_model: database exceptions, timeouts, connectivity faults and Byzantine/corrupted responses
empirical_method: tool design and demonstration with empirical evaluation context
data_source: Filibuster extension, IDE plugin and supported database-client scenarios
participants_or_subjects: developers are intended users; no direct participant study reported
metrics_or_outcomes: fault types supported; locations and impacts visualised; resilience tests can be generated at development time
human_factors: developer feedback is a tool feature, not a validated workload or decision measure
reproducibility_information: author version, tool integration and supported database technologies are reported; benchmark/configuration details require further extraction
limitations_or_scope: companion paper and tool evaluation; no production recovery or human comparison

citation: Jiang et al. (2024), Xpert: Empowering Incident Management with Query Recommendations via Large Language Models

fault_or_incident_model: historical incidents and KQL queries used for offline evaluation; production deployment reported

participants_or_subjects: on-call engineers are users; no controlled participant comparison
metrics_or_outcomes: query recommendation quality including Xcore-style evaluation and production use; exact values require charting
human_factors: query use provides operational-work context but does not directly measure workload, trust or decision quality
reproducibility_information: arXiv full text and code/data availability claims require detailed extraction; production data are proprietary

operational_context: large-scale cloud operations and postmortem analysis
fault_or_incident_model: production incident tickets and hierarchical fault-pattern labels

participants_or_subjects: engineers perform or consume profiling; no direct participant sample
metrics_or_outcomes: classification performance; more than 10,000 incidents analysed; fault trends reported from deployment
human_factors: manual-labelling burden is discussed; no direct workload/trust instrument
reproducibility_information: public record describes data scale and deployment; proprietary CloudA data limit replication

citation: Yang et al. (2024), MicroRes: Versatile Resilience Profiling in Microservices via Degradation Dissemination Indexing

fault_or_incident_model: injected failures and propagation from system-performance to user-aware metrics

metrics_or_outcomes: resilience index based on degradation dissemination; comparative evaluation across three systems
reproducibility_information: arXiv and author repository identify code/artefacts; exact scenarios, reset and metric definitions require extraction
